videos.script: Anthropic's agent library is not a loop written in Python. It is Claude Code itself, the command-line agent, started as a subprocess and driven from your program. {{title}} That has consequences you can measure. Left at its defaults, the first request of a two-step answer carried twenty-three tools and thirteen and a half thousand tokens, nearly all of them Claude Code's own. One option takes that to three tools and four hundred tokens. {{wire}} It also reads a CLAUDE.md file if one is in the working directory. Its permission system has several layers: which tools exist, which are allowed, a mode, a callback for a person, and hooks that run before every call. {{layers}} You will put a person in front of a refund, refuse a large one in code before anybody is asked, and keep an audit line of every call. {{refund}} And last, the turn limit, and sessions that a second message can resume, which leave the conversation in files on disk. {{last}}
